basis: Copper transport defect with defining skeletal and neurologic disease; bladder diverticula 4/4. Skin, GI, vascular and hepatic involvement omitted at cap.

decisions.neurologic: primary: neurodegeneration is in the supplied definition; developmental delay 4/4 and intellectual disability 80-99% support a defining neurologic phenotype.

basis: Proteus infections predominantly affect the urinary tract (>30%); direct cystitis or pyelonephritis supports urinary-organ involvement.

decisions.renal: involved: urinary infections are the predominant clinical presentation (>30%); these are direct Proteus infections, rather than a later disease risk.

basis: Defining developmental disability and obesity; strabismus 2/3, refractive impairment 30-79%, hip dysplasia 1/3. Laryngeal cleft 1/3 omitted at cap; pigment spots do not impair skin.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: hip dysplasia in 1/3 meets the supplied approximately 30% threshold and represents structural joint disease; evidence comes from a small sample.

basis: Hindbrain malformation; skeletal findings (30-79%) are associated anomalies or secondary scoliosis. Vestibular findings (30-79%) do not establish direct inner-ear damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: vertebral anomalies are associated malformations; scoliosis is secondary and separately diagnosed. The 30-79% annotations do not establish direct skeletal injury.
decisions.otologic: none: vestibular symptoms and eighth-nerve abnormalities are predominantly neurologic; 30-79% functional annotations do not establish direct, persistent ear damage.

basis: Thoracic/cervical skeletal and auricular malformations define the syndrome. Cleft lip/palate, cardiac defects and ptosis have unspecified frequencies and unestablished diagnostic status.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: cleft lip/palate has no supplied frequency or established status as a major diagnostic criterion; facial dysmorphism alone does not establish gastrointestinal disease.

basis: Site-unspecified umbrella; hepatic assignment is provisional from the usual clinical entity. Hepatic and subcutaneous subtypes limit certainty; mesenchymal histology does not prove locomotor origin.

decisions.hepatic: primary: provisional assignment to the usual hepatic presentation of mesenchymal hamartoma; the site-unspecified umbrella and nonhepatic child make this uncertain.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: mesenchymal histology alone does not establish bone, joint, skeletal muscle or locomotor connective-tissue origin; no such site is specified.

basis: Retinal dystrophy, obesity and renal disease are major Bardet-Biedl criteria; renal failure and intellectual disability each 1/1 in this subtype. Brachydactyly omitted at cap.

decisions.renal: primary: renal disease is a major Bardet-Biedl diagnostic feature, with renal insufficiency and stage 5 kidney disease documented in the reported subtype case (1/1).

basis: Phytanic acid disorder with defining retinal degeneration and neuropathy/ataxia; cardiomyopathy annotated 80-99%. Common hearing, skin and skeletal involvement omitted at cap.

decisions.neurologic: primary: polyneuropathy, anosmia and ataxia are defining diagnostic manifestations; neuropathy/ataxia are annotated 80-99%.
decisions.ocular: primary: early-onset retinitis pigmentosa explicitly characterizes the disease and is a major diagnostic feature; retinal disease is annotated 80-99%.

basis: Contractures and impaired proprioception define the disease. Respiratory insufficiency (6/6) is typically transient neonatal dysfunction, without established lasting lung or airway damage.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory insufficiency in 6/6 is typically neonatal and transient, reflecting neuromuscular dysfunction rather than demonstrated lasting pulmonary injury.

basis: Pituitary deficiency and immunodeficiency define disease; alopecia/nail dystrophy occur in 30-79%. Bronchiectasis (30-79%) follows separately diagnosed respiratory infections.

decisions.pulmonary: none: bronchiectasis (30-79%) is secondary to separately diagnosed recurrent respiratory infections; neither establishes direct pulmonary involvement by this syndrome.
